title_en: Visions of the Future (19/20): Smart Cities, Ideal and Reality
note_en: 不在于…而在于… means "the point lies not in A but in B" and is used to correct a common assumption about what really matters: 真正的智慧或许不在于城市有多少传感器，而在于它能不能让普通人的生活变得更方便. Notice that both halves are followed by whole clauses, including embedded questions (有多少…, 能不能…), which English turns into "how many…" and "whether…".

sentences.en: Walking a little farther, they came to a stand with two city models side by side: one glittered with the lights of countless sensors, like a future city from a science-fiction movie, while the other looked quite ordinary, with just a few small labels stuck on its streetlights and trash cans. Xiao Le pointed at the ordinary one and asked why both were called "smart cities" when they looked completely different.

sentences.en: Xiao Le said this was a lot like the "moving to Mars" exhibit they had just seen: at first everyone wanted to build a brand-new, perfect future, and only later did they discover that what can really be achieved is usually fixing up what's right in front of you, bit by bit. Grandpa nodded and said, "That's right. Whether it's cities, rockets, or anything else, in the end people usually don't paint a perfect dream in one go; they build the parts that are truly useful, one small piece at a time."
